note: QUIRK titles are already full sentences, so a description that restates the behavior adds nothing. Each of these supplies the why, the cost, or the consequence instead -- matched to the existing rows, e.g. Allergies: 'The world contains substances that have opinions about this entity.'

entries.title: Always leaves a breadcrumb trail wherever they go.
entries.description: Not for finding the way back. For proving they were there, to somebody who has not arrived yet.

entries.title: Always speaks in riddles.
entries.description: Direct answers are available and have been ruled out. The listener is expected to earn it, every single time.

entries.title: Always starts conversations by quoting obscure poetry.
entries.description: The opener is a filter. Anyone who recognises the line is worth continuing with; anyone who does not gets it explained.

entries.title: Always wears mismatched socks intentionally.
entries.description: The mismatch is curated. There is a correct way to be wrong about this and getting it wrong twice would defeat the purpose.

entries.title: Believes staring contests determine trustworthiness.
entries.description: Holds the gaze well past comfort and draws real conclusions from the result. Those conclusions have been right often enough to continue.

entries.title: Believes that certain colors bring them good luck.
entries.description: The list is specific, private, and has been revised exactly once. That revision is not discussed.

entries.title: Believes that sneezing wards off evil spirits.
entries.description: Treats every sneeze as a small service performed for the room. Says nothing, expects no thanks, considers the matter handled.

entries.title: Believes their shadow is plotting against them.
entries.description: Keeps it in view at all times. It has never done anything, which is exactly what a patient conspirator would arrange.

entries.title: Can juggle but only uses fruits.
entries.description: Balls were available and have been declined. The stakes are lower with fruit and considerably funnier when it goes wrong.

entries.title: Can mimic the sound of any animal perfectly.
entries.description: Convincing enough to fool the animal. This has caused problems nobody anticipated and none of them have been repeated.

entries.title: Can’t resist counting things aloud.
entries.description: Loses the thread of a conversation to a staircase, a row of windows, a bowl of anything. Resumes without acknowledging the gap.

entries.title: Can’t resist making puns in dire situations.
entries.description: The timing is not accidental. Something in them insists on lowering the temperature, and it has occasionally worked.

entries.title: Carries a candle everywhere "just in case."
entries.description: The case has arrived twice. Both times everyone else was extremely glad about the candle and said so out loud.

entries.title: Carries a compass but never uses it.
entries.description: Knows where north is without it. Carries one because a person who might need a compass is a person with somewhere to go.

entries.title: Carries a pocket full of acorns for "emergencies."
entries.description: No emergency has yet required an acorn. This is not treated as evidence against the practice.

entries.title: Carries an empty journal for "recording important events."
entries.description: Nothing has qualified yet. The standard is high on purpose, and the blank pages are the point rather than a failure.

entries.title: Collects buttons from every town they visit.
entries.description: One per town, chosen rather than found. The collection is a map that only they can read.

entries.title: Collects feathers and treats them as treasure.
entries.description: Sorted, named, and stored with more care than most people give currency. The valuation is internally consistent.

entries.title: Compulsively organizes objects by size.
entries.description: Hands move before the decision does. Other people's shelves are a source of quiet, ongoing suffering.

entries.title: Constantly names inanimate objects.
entries.description: The kettle has a name and a temperament. Anyone who mocks this gets corrected gently and at considerable length.

entries.title: Constantly sketches "the same recurring dream."
entries.description: The drawing changes slightly each time, which means either the dream is moving or the hand is. Neither answer is comforting.

entries.title: Doodles elaborate maps of imaginary lands.
entries.description: Coastlines, trade routes, and a scale bar. The lands are not real and the geography is nonetheless consistent.

entries.title: Gets distracted by shiny objects mid-conversation.
entries.description: Mid-sentence, gone. Returns with no memory of the sentence and total recall of the object.

entries.title: Gives names to every stray cat they encounter.
entries.description: The names stick, at least on their side of the arrangement. Several of the cats have started answering to them.

entries.title: Has a pet rock they insist is sentient.
entries.description: Presents no evidence and requires none. The rock has been consulted on major decisions and has not yet been wrong.

entries.title: Has a strong aversion to mirrors.
entries.description: Will cross a room to avoid one. There is a reason, and nobody has ever asked in a way that deserved to hear it.

entries.title: Has a superstition about only stepping on cracks.
entries.description: On the cracks, deliberately, which inverts the usual arrangement. Nobody has asked what happens if they miss one.

entries.title: Has a superstition about wearing mismatched gloves.
entries.description: Matching gloves are considered an unnecessary risk. The specifics of that risk have never been made public.

entries.title: Has trained themselves to remember everything in rhyme.
entries.description: Everything important is stored as verse. Recall is flawless and the retrieval is audible from the next room.

entries.title: Invents elaborate backstories for people they meet.
entries.description: Full histories assigned inside a minute of meeting. Occasionally checked against reality, and the accuracy rate is unsettling.

entries.title: Invents riddles for strangers and expects answers.
entries.description: Poses it, waits, and does not fill the silence. The waiting is the part people remember afterward.

entries.title: Is a professional finger snapper, complete with routines.
entries.description: There are routines. There is a warm-up. Against every reasonable expectation it is genuinely impressive to watch.

entries.title: Keeps an invisible "force field" around themselves.
entries.description: Maintains a precise personal radius and adjusts it for the room. Everyone senses the boundary without being told where it sits.

entries.title: Knows an absurd amount of facts about frogs.
entries.description: Unprompted, endless, and correct. The frogs have done nothing to earn this and would not understand it if they had.

entries.title: Knows an absurd amount of trivia about cheese.
entries.description: Regional, historical, and entirely unsolicited. Has ruined at least one dinner party and measurably improved two others.

entries.title: Laughs at their own jokes before finishing them.
entries.description: The joke rarely arrives intact. The laugh is good enough that the room usually joins in regardless.

entries.title: Laughs uncontrollably at the mention of pickles.
entries.description: No explanation has ever been offered. The reaction is immediate, total, and has survived every attempt to suppress it.

entries.title: Leaves cryptic notes in bottles wherever they go.
entries.description: Writes to nobody in particular and means every word. Somewhere out there is a person quietly collecting them.

entries.title: Obsessed with finding "the perfect stick."
entries.description: Has held thousands and kept none. The search is the relationship; finding it would end something.

entries.title: Only communicates through song when nervous.
entries.description: The nerves route through the singing instead of the speech. It is disarming, which is presumably why it survived this long.

entries.title: Only drinks tea that’s been stirred counterclockwise.
entries.description: The direction matters. Anyone who stirs it the other way is quietly never asked to make tea again.

entries.title: Only eats foods in alphabetical order.
entries.description: Plans the whole plate before touching any of it. A dessert beginning with A has caused genuine difficulty.

entries.title: Only walks in the shadows, avoiding direct sunlight.
entries.description: Moves along the shaded side of everything. Not a condition and not an aversion, simply a route that has always been theirs.

entries.title: Only wears boots, even in formal settings.
entries.description: The boots are polished. The boots are appropriate. Everyone else's opinion on the boots has been noted and set aside.

entries.title: Refuses to cross bridges without whistling a tune.
entries.description: Always the same tune. Whether it works has never been tested, and testing it is not on the table.

entries.title: Refuses to sit on chairs with cushions.
entries.description: Takes the hard one by choice and stays comfortable long after everyone in the soft ones has started shifting.

entries.title: Refuses to touch books with even page numbers.
entries.description: Turns two at a time when it comes to it. Has read a great many books and can tell you nothing about half of them.

entries.title: Refuses to touch objects made of copper.
entries.description: Coins get handled through a sleeve. Nobody has established what copper did, and asking has never produced a straight answer.

entries.title: Sniffs books to judge their "character."
entries.description: Judges a book before reading a word of it, and is right more often than the method has any right to be.

entries.title: Sprinkles salt around their bed before sleeping.
entries.description: A thin unbroken line, checked before lying down. Sleeps extremely well, which complicates any argument against the practice.

entries.title: Takes "invisible notes" with a pretend quill.
entries.description: The quill is not there. The notes are apparently detailed, and they have been quoted back accurately more than once.

entries.title: Talks to doors before opening them.
entries.description: A short greeting first. Considers it basic manners toward something that spends all day letting people through.

entries.title: Terrified of butterflies but loves moths.
entries.description: The distinction is absolute and the reasoning is unavailable. Moths are welcome to land wherever they like.

entries.title: Uses completely nonsensical phrases as insults.
entries.description: Invented on the spot and landing regardless. Nobody has managed to be properly offended and nobody has managed not to be.

entries.title: Uses overly dramatic hand gestures for mundane tasks.
entries.description: Fetches a glass of water like a curtain call. Nothing is small when they do it, which is exhausting and slightly wonderful.

entries.title: Wears a scarf year-round, even in summer.
entries.description: Summer changes nothing at all. The scarf is load-bearing in a way that has never been explained to anybody.

entries.title: Wears mismatched earrings to "confuse the spirits."
entries.description: The asymmetry is the working part. Spirits are said to find it disorienting, and no spirit has yet complained.

entries.title: Whispers to the moon before going to sleep.
entries.description: A short report, delivered quietly, every night. The moon has never replied and the reports have never stopped.

entries.title: Writes letters to fictional characters.
entries.description: Sealed, addressed, and kept in a drawer. Some of them are apologies, which is the part that stays with you.

entries.title: Writes poetry on any available surface.
entries.description: Receipts, walls, the fog on a window. The impulse does not wait for paper and never has.
